topic: Process Synthesis - the Pioneering Contributions of Jeffrey J. Siirola
title: Process Synthesis - the Pioneering Contributions of Jeffrey J. Siirola
session_title: 10A: Session in Honor of Jeff Siirola on His 80th Birthday
abstract: Chemical engineers, and our forebears, have conceptualized and built chemical processes for centuries. Many of the early processes could be described as a recipe for taking valuable raw materials and turning them mostly into toxic waste. During the 20th century, a more systematic, and successful, approach emerged that we call Process Synthesis. The formal beginning of the field of process synthesis can be easily dated to the landmark book titled, Process Synthesis, by Rudd, Powers and Siirola, published in 1973. In this presentation, we pay tribute to more than 60 years of research and development in the field by Jeffrey Siirola.

topic: Systems Thinking for the Energy Transition: Celebrating Jeff Siirola’s Legacy and Charting Purdue’s Energy Vision
title: Systems Thinking for the Energy Transition: Celebrating Jeff Siirola’s Legacy and Charting Purdue’s Energy Vision
session_title: 10A: Session in Honor of Jeff Siirola on His 80th Birthday
abstract: This talk celebrates the 80th birthday of Professor Jeffrey J. Siirola and shows how his process-systems mindset continues to guide the energy transition. For five decades Jeff has fused techno-economic analysis with molecular-scale insight, charting new, cost-effective pathways for fuels and chemicals. His counsel has been decisive in three Purdue-led efforts: in the NSF ERC CISTAR he defined value-driven routes for light-alkane upgrading; for the proposed Manufacturing Innovation Institute ELECTRIFY he quantified the economic and emissions benefits of electrified process heat; and within the college-wide LEAPS initiative he mentors teams pursuing affordable, reliable, and sustainable energy through nuclear innovation, grid modernization, and circular-carbon strategies. From these examples one enduring lesson emerges: start with system-wide economics, then pinpoint the technology gaps and focused research needed to close them—making elegance serve relevance. Extending Jeff Siirola’s systems perspective to today’s frontiers can power a more equitable and prosperous energy future. The reflection concludes with priorities for the coming decade, emphasizing open-source digital frameworks and cross-sector partnerships.

topic: Using New Tricks to Help Old Dogs: How Technology Helped Explain a Decades-Old Incident.
title: Using New Tricks to Help Old Dogs: How Technology Helped Explain a Decades-Old Incident.
session_title: 10A: Session in Honor of Jeff Siirola on His 80th Birthday
abstract: In this session, the application of Residue Curve mapping, a technology targeting distillation and process synthesis, to a 1960 explosion will show how advances in analytical methods can be applied in unique ways to help understand historical process safety events. Dr. Siirola was instrumental in both the development of the technique, and the analysis of the incident in question.

topic: Contributions By Jeff Siirola to Carnegie Mellon University Research and Education in Process Systems Engineering
title: Contributions By Jeff Siirola to Carnegie Mellon University Research and Education in Process Systems Engineering
session_title: 10A: Session in Honor of Jeff Siirola on His 80th Birthday
abstract: In this presentation we will describe the huge impact that Dr. Jeff Siirola has had on the research and teaching of process design at Carnegie Mellon University, and in the area of Process Systems Engineering at large. At Carnegie Mellon we were extremely fortunate to have had very meaningful interactions with Jeff Siirola through the membership of Eastman Chemical to our Center for Advanced Process Decision-making (CAPD) and to the Engineering Design Research Center. Through our interactions with him he promoted the development of new ideas and approaches in the areas of process synthesis, separation and heat integration systems, conceptual design, design theory /methodology, process development, sustainable development, and carbon management. We were also very fortunate to having interacted with Jeff Siirola through our senior design course where over 20 years he has provided every year a unique and relevant design project for the senior design course. In addition, he has given several lectures in that course on process synthesis and process safety. Also, during a two-year period, in which he was part time faculty at Carnegie Mellon, he put together the unique course entitled “Chemical Process Technology,” which we were very fortunate to tape as it is truly a gem in chemical engineering education. The course provides a comprehensive view on the evolution of the chemical industry, emphasizing major technology changes and sustainability issues. https://www.cheme.engineering.cmu.edu/education/online-course.html

topic: Jeff Siirola's Educational Contributions to Process Systems Engineering at Purdue
title: Jeff Siirola's Educational Contributions to Process Systems Engineering at Purdue
session_title: 10A: Session in Honor of Jeff Siirola on His 80th Birthday
abstract: Over the past decade, Purdue has had one of the largest graduating senior classes in chemical engineering, typically numbering in the mid-range between one hundred and two hundred students. The size of is this student body has allowed Jeff to create a classroom format for the capstone process/plant design course featuring a large numbers of teams and unleashing their creative forces to explore a wide range of feasible solutions to challenging problems in process design. Since 2017 and the onset of the NSF Engineering Research Center for Innovative and Strategic Transformation of Alkane Resources (CISTAR), the design projects revolved around the many opportunities associated with capturing the value of stranded light hydrocarbons from the shale oil revolution. This talk will feature some of the highlights from these courses, including additional insights from offering the capstone design course in fall semester as well as the traditional format in the spring semester.

topic: Thermodynamics, Sinking Trees and Aiche Restructuring
title: Thermodynamics, Sinking Trees and Aiche Restructuring
session_title: 10A: Session in Honor of Jeff Siirola on His 80th Birthday
abstract: Leading significant structural changes to the world’s energy systems is certainly more challenging than reviving a 100-year-old professional society, but both require detailed analysis and creativity. Jeff has made significant contributions in both areas. We’ll talk about how he helped lead AIChE from a financially struggling organization to one with strong financials while also initiating strategic growth opportunities.

topic: Planning and Scheduling of CACHE-Sponsored Conferences Under Uncertainty
title: Planning and Scheduling of CACHE-Sponsored Conferences Under Uncertainty
session_title: 10A: Session in Honor of Jeff Siirola on His 80th Birthday
abstract: Jeff Siirola has been a Trustee of CACHE (Computer Aids for Chemical Engineering) since 1984. He served as the organizations President from 1990-1992. Jeff has had many accomplishments in CACHE, but what he is probably best known for is his leadership in executing dozens of “Foundations of...” conferences sponsored by CACHE. He was able to draw upon his planning and scheduling training as a systems engineer to help CACHE build an outstanding portfolio of conferences that are known for their outstanding quality. Moreover, he built a sustainable model that has allowed these conferences to thrive. In this talk, we will review some of the milestones from Jeff’s conference planning activities.

topic: An ABET Multipotentialite: Jeff’s Journey through ABET.
title: An ABET Multipotentialite: Jeff’s Journey through ABET.
session_title: 10A: Session in Honor of Jeff Siirola on His 80th Birthday
abstract: Jeff’s participation in ABET has involved a large number of roles including program evaluator, commissioner, AIChE society liaison to ABET, member of board of directors, and secretary (two terms). As the AIChE society liaison to ABET, Jeff also served as chair of the AIChE Education and Accreditation (E&A) Committee. Along with his many roles within ABET, Jeff’s near-decade journey in leading the AIChE E&A committee will be highlighted, with an emphasis on his leadership in navigating several challenges and opportunities that included the expansion of ABET visits to international locations and the need to enhance safety awareness in chemical engineering programs.
